requirement:
Each decorator on a selectable declaration is a separate `Annotation` owned
by that declaration. Stacked decorators follow the source order specified by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.order`.
rationale:
The test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[typescript_and_tsx_decorators_belong_to_the_decorated_declaration]` is marked `{test}` for `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.attachments.decorators`. It covers each obligation in the requirement text.

- **Separate `Annotation` per decorator, owned by the decorated declaration.** The test collects `(item.selector, &source[attachment.span])` for every attachment on every item. It asserts `attachment.kind == Annotation` for each one. It then compares the full list of records. `@sealed` and `@register("widget")` are separate records owned by `class[Widget]`. `@trace` and the multi-line `@metrics.time(...)` are separate records owned by `class[Widget]/method[render]`. `@published(...)` is owned by `class[Base]`, a class with `export default abstract`. `@local` is owned by the nested `class[Base]/class[Local]`, not by `Base`.
- **Source order for stacked decorators** (`requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.order`, cited). The expected list is an ordered slice, so it fixes the order for both the stacked class decorators and the stacked method decorators.
- **Only selectable declarations own decorators.** The `@field` field decorator and the `@input` parameter decorator are absent from the expected records. `plain()` has no attachments. This checks that decorators on non-selectable members are not attached.
- **Both dialects.** The loop runs over `widget.ts` and `widget.tsx`.

The fingerprint and structural-hash assertions go beyond this requirement. They are covered by other requirements that the test also marks.

The tests rule out plausible violating behaviors: merged decorators, wrong owners, reversed order, and decorators attached to the wrong declaration. I found no unexercised obligation or boundary that the text names.
